item.title: Backloggd urges password changes following security breach and admin tool exploitation
item.description:
Source: Engadget Original headline: Backloggd urges users to change their passwords after a breach
Video game-logging site Backloggd has urged users to change their passwords following a security breach. Administrator MrProg reported on November 25 that an attacker exploited a bug to gain access to the site's admin tools, exposing usernames, email addresses, hashed passwords, and IP addresses. Payment information was not compromised because it is handled through Patreon. While the platform uses a strong hashing method, MrProg noted that weak or common passwords can sometimes be guessed from their hashes. The administrator temporarily took the site offline to fix the bug and lock out the attacker, who had hidden games and restricted certain accounts. MrProg is reverting all changes made by the attacker and confirmed that game logs, reviews, and lists remain intact. The site, which recently reached 1 million users, has added stricter access to admin tools to prevent future incidents. MrProg is currently seeking legal guidance and plans to share a full notice with more details soon.

item.title: Google fixes issue causing Gemini tab to use excessive Chrome memory
item.description:
Source: Digital Trends Original headline: Google says Gemini in Chrome will no longer bring your computer to a crawl
Google has confirmed a fix for a memory issue where running a Gemini tab in Chrome could consume more than 6GB of RAM. The company's official support account addressed the problem following a Reddit complaint regarding Gemini using over 5GB of memory. While Google has not specified the cause of the high memory usage, users can monitor or manage RAM consumption using Chrome's built-in Task Manager, accessible via Shift + Esc on Windows or Linux. This tool allows users to view memory usage for individual tabs and extensions, or end specific processes to free up resources. Additionally, Chrome offers a Memory Saver feature under Settings > Performance that deactivates inactive tabs to preserve RAM. Although Google states the issue is resolved, the fix has not yet been independently verified, and users may still notice sluggishness if Gemini or other tabs occupy significant memory.

item.title: Hera mission images show DART impact created stadium-sized crater on Dimorphos
item.description:
Source: Gizmodo Original headline: NASA’s DART Mission Left a Stadium-Sized Crater on an Asteroid. And We Just Got the Pictures to Prove It
New images from the European Space Agency's Hera mission reveal that NASA's 2022 DART impact left a stadium-sized crater on the asteroid Dimorphos. The impact, which occurred at nearly 15,000 miles per hour, flattened one side of the 558-foot-wide rock and sent it into a chaotic tumble. Observations also show that the collision scattered hundreds of previously unknown boulders around the binary asteroid system, which includes the larger companion Didymos. Hera, which launched on October 7, 2024, arrived at the site three weeks ago and is currently 19 miles away. Hera principal investigator Patrick Michel stated that the impact caused Dimorphos to sustain a crater, change its shape, and stay the same, noting the surprise at these simultaneous effects. The mission will continue to examine the asteroids over the next six months, eventually deploying miniature satellites Milani and Juventas in early 2027 to study material composition and internal structures via radar.

item.title: 1Password attacker steals certain customer data but leaves user vaults and passwords safe
item.description:
Source: Engadget Original headline: 1Password says it was hacked but users' vaults are safe
1Password confirmed an attacker infiltrated its system after compromising an employee's corporate GitHub account on November 19. The attacker used this access to reach source code and inject malicious code into the company's backend. While the breach allowed the theft of certain customer data, including names, email addresses, account creation dates, last sign-in times, and public keys, 1Password maintains that user vaults and logins remain secure. The company does not have access to actual passwords, recovery keys, or the secret keys that protect vaults, meaning those credentials were not stolen. "Your vault data, the items in them, and the keys that protect them are safe and were not affected," the company stated. In response, 1Password revoked the stolen token, disabled the affected GitHub account, and implemented new detection tools. Although vault data is safe, the company warns that compromised email addresses could facilitate phishing attempts via fake account recovery and invitation emails.

item.title: Archaeologists find papyrus fragments documenting ancient Egyptian rituals to defeat Apophis
item.description:
Source: Gizmodo Original headline: Archaeologists Find Rare Evidence of Ancient Egyptians’ Ritual Battle Against Apophis
Archaeologists have discovered 40 charred and pierced papyrus fragments at a temple in ancient Thebes that provide physical evidence of the "Apophis ritual." Dating back roughly 3,000 years, these remnants detail a ceremony used to symbolically defeat Apophis, the god of chaos, who threatened the sun god Ra. According to instructions in "A Book of Overthrowing Apophis," priests would stab, trample, and burn representations of the deity to maintain universal order. The fragments, found in a trash dump, show signs of being pierced and consumed by fire, matching ritual instructions. Lead author Fredrik Hagen, a professor of Egyptology at the University of Copenhagen, stated that the finds indicate these rituals were a regular part of temple life and likely a common feature of Egyptian culture more broadly. While previously thought to be reserved for religious leaders, the discovery suggests that literate non-priests also accessed such magic for protection or to curse enemies. Researchers suggest the ritual may have been performed on at least 20 separate occasions.

item.title: Apple may produce limited-edition ceramic iPhone 20 Pro
item.description:
Source: Digital Trends Original headline: Apple may be planning a limited-edition ceramic iPhone 20 Pro
Apple may produce a limited-edition ceramic iPhone 20 Pro, according to leaks from Fixed Focus Digital. The source claims to have touched ceramic components intended for the device, though it remains unclear if the material would be used for a rear panel or part of the enclosure. Production capacity for such a model would be very low, and the design must pass engineering validation testing before entering mass production. While Apple currently uses Ceramic Shield glass on certain models and ceramic casings on Apple Watch Series 12, a full ceramic iPhone would likely be heavier and more difficult to manufacture. Competitors like Xiaomi, OnePlus, and Huawei have previously used ceramic casings, noting the material's hardness and the complex, high-temperature baking processes required. If Apple releases 20th-anniversary models, they are expected in fall 2027. The scarcity of a ceramic iPhone 20 Pro could potentially increase its future resale value.

item.title: Enough phone project increases battery, storage, and RAM without raising backer price
item.description:
Source: PCMag Original headline: This Compact Phone Project Upped Storage and RAM Without a Price Hike
The Enough phone, a Kickstarter project for a compact Android device, has increased its technical specifications without raising the price for current backers. The device features a 5.3-inch display, similar in size to the iPhone 12 mini, and will run Android 17 with support through 2032. While original plans listed a 3,500mAh battery, 128GB of storage, and 8GB of RAM, the updated specifications now include a 3,850mAh battery, 256GB of storage, and 12GB of RAM. The phone will use a MediaTek Dimensity 7500 chip, a 50MP rear camera with a Sony IMX766 sensor, and a 32MP selfie camera. Backers can currently secure the device for $499, with early bird pricing previously available at $399. The planned retail price is $599. The project targets a May 2027 release for its first wave of deliveries.

item.title: Thermal Grizzly releases Delid-Heat-Mate tool for oven-based CPU delidding
item.description:
Source: Latest from Tom's Hardware Original headline: New delidding tool helps you bake your CPU in the oven to remove heatspreader
Thermal Grizzly has released the Delid-Heat-Mate, a CNC-machined aluminum tool designed to assist in the CPU delidding process. After using a Delid-Die-Mate to loosen the integrated heat spreader (IHS), users place the CPU in the Delid-Heat-Mate with the heat spreader facing down and heat it in an oven. This heat liquefies the indium solder, allowing the IHS to drop away under its own weight. This method is less mechanically stressful than using a delidding tool alone, reducing the risk of chipping the CPU die or prying off small components. The Delid-Heat-Mate is compatible with AMD AM5 and Intel LGA 1700, 1851, and 1954 sockets and costs $23.28. This provides a more affordable and universal alternative to the Delid-Die-Mate Heater, which costs $127.41 and is limited to Intel LGA 1851 socket CPUs.

item.title: Ninm Lab releases transparent portable CD player with detachable Bluetooth speaker
item.description:
Source: New Atlas Original headline: Crystal-clear CD player adds on detachable Bluetooth speaker
Ninm Lab has announced the Long Time No See Too, a transparent portable CD player featuring a detachable circular magnetic Bluetooth speaker. Available in Translucent White or Vivid Red, the 84.2 g speaker module includes a built-in subwoofer designed to deliver deeper bass than the original model. The new device features two-way Bluetooth 5.3, allowing users to transmit audio from a smartphone to the player or send CD audio to wireless headphones. It also includes a 3.5-mm output, a new LED display for playback information, and USB-C charging, though two AA batteries remain an option. While the player supports standard CDs, CD-Rs, and CD-RWs, anti-shock protection has been reduced from 60 seconds to 15 seconds, though MP3 playback maintains 120 seconds of protection. The device is available through Ninm Lab’s website for HK$988, or approximately US$127. This follows the original model, which raised HK$732,450 from 872 Kickstarter backers in 2020.

item.title: University of Southern California engineers build smart ring that detects stress with 92% accuracy
item.description:
Source: New Atlas Original headline: The ultimate mood ring senses your stress before you - with 92% accuracy
Engineers at the University of Southern California have developed a smart ring that detects stress by monitoring sweat gland activity using infrared radiation. Unlike traditional mood rings that rely on temperature, this device uses two infrared LEDs—one at 960 nanometers and another at 1,250 nm—to measure skin moisture and blood flow. By combining these signals with a temperature sensor, an accelerometer, and a machine-learning model, the ring attempts to distinguish between mental stress and physical exertion. In lab tests involving six volunteers, the device identified cold-water stress with 92% accuracy, outperforming gel-based electrosensors which reached only 78%. In a 12-hour experiment, the ring maintained roughly 80% accuracy in distinguishing stress from rest. Researcher Yasser Khan and his colleagues plan to conduct further testing with 40 people in an office setting over one year to better refine the software's ability to untangle overlapping signals like deadlines and physical activity. The research was published in Science Advances.

item.title: INSTRUCTION: Dedicated software tools enable conversion of PDF files to editable Word documents
item.description:
Source: PCWorld Original headline: How do I convert a PDF to a Word document?
Converting a PDF to a Microsoft Word document requires dedicated software to preserve layout, tables, and text structure, as simple copy-and-paste methods often break formatting or fail to recognize unsupported fonts. Using Adobe Acrobat, users can convert a file to a DOCX format by selecting the PDF to Word tool and uploading the document. For scanned PDFs, which lack a native text layer, converters must use Optical Character Recognition (OCR) to extract and create editable text. While free online tools or free tiers of software like Adobe Acrobat can handle simple, text-heavy files, more complex documents containing tables, graphs, or multi-column layouts require advanced engines found in premium versions like Adobe Acrobat Pro. These professional tools use document-layout detection and formula recognition to rebuild gridlines and maintain correct paragraph spacing. For those needing to handle high volumes of sophisticated or scanned documents, subscription-based services provide the necessary speed and accuracy to ensure the resulting Word document retains the original shape and flow.

item.title: New apps enable iPhone Duo to function as a laptop
item.description:
Source: Digital Trends Original headline: The iPhone Duo can now double as a laptop thanks to these apps
New software updates allow the iPhone Duo to function as a compact laptop. Edovia released Screens version 5.10.6, which introduces a Laptop Mode. When the device is folded, the top half displays a remote desktop while the bottom half provides a custom keyboard and trackpad. This mode works with High Performance Screen Sharing to fit a remote Mac desktop onto the top half of the device, offering improved graphics and audio, particularly when connected to a Mac with Apple silicon running macOS 14 Sonoma or later. Additionally, Code with Beto released Nimvo version 1.2, which includes fold-aware layouts for the iPhone Duo. Nimvo 1.2 provides Mac audio, a shared clipboard, and file transfers, requiring iOS 27.1 or later for fold-aware layouts. Screens 5.10.6 is available via a 7-day trial, a $4.99 monthly plan, a $29.99 yearly plan, or a $249.99 lifetime purchase. Nimvo costs $24.99 per year or $49.99 for lifetime access in the US.

item.title: Osolabs develops modular 6502 computer for learning hardware architecture
item.description:
Source: Hackaday Original headline: A Modular 6502 Computer
The 20c from [osolabs] is a modular learning platform designed to teach computer architecture at a low level. Unlike traditional compact microcomputers, the 20c uses interchangeable modules that correspond to key architectural components. Users can swap CPU modules, such as the 6502, 6510, or 8502, and replace modules for ROM, RAM, address and data buses, and clock or glue logic. The system even supports I/O subsystem modules like the Commodore PIA, VIA, and CIA. By assembling and swapping these pieces, builders can create machines with different characters to learn how hardware functions. Design files for the project are available on Github for those interested in the technical specifications.

item.title: INSTRUCTION: Mini PC and local network setup provide offline internet alternatives
item.description:
Source: How-To Geek Original headline: A $300 mini PC can keep your home network alive when internet and cellular both fail
A local area network (LAN) can function independently of the internet, allowing devices to exchange files and access local services even when an ISP or cellular connection fails. By using a mini PC, such as an Intel N100 with 8GB of RAM, a router, and an Ethernet cable, a user can build a capable offline network. Installing operating systems like Debian or Ubuntu Server allows the mini PC to host services like Samba for file sharing, Jellyfin for streaming downloaded movies, and Kiwix for hosting offline copies of Wikipedia. To ensure reliability, the mini PC should be assigned a reserved IP address via DHCP. For a truly resilient setup, both the mini PC and networking equipment, including switches and access points, should be connected to a UPS or portable power station to prevent a power outage from disabling the network. Users should test the setup by disconnecting the WAN cable to confirm that local services remain accessible.

item.title: INSTRUCTION: Four kitchen gadgets can be built using an ESP32 microcontroller
item.description:
Source: How-To Geek Original headline: 4 useful kitchen gadgets you can make with an ESP32 this weekend (Nov 27 - 29)
The ESP32 microcontroller can be used to build several functional kitchen gadgets. A digital kitchen timer can be constructed using an M5Stack Dial or a Cheap Yellow Display, both of which support ESPHome for integration with Home Assistant to trigger smart home alerts like flashing lights or smart speaker notifications. For a low-cost smart scale, blogger Liore Shai demonstrates how to convert a $10 Amazon Basics scale using a $5 ESP32, a load cell amplifier, and an I2C OLED screen to produce a web interface with JSON responses. A smart spice rack can be built using an ESP32, 3D-printed holders, and 330 LEDs, where a web interface lights up the LED under a specific spice jar. Finally, wireless temperature probes can be made using an ESP32 connected to a barbecue-type probe and a resistor, or specialized versions like a pizza oven thermometer. These devices can be calibrated with reliable thermometers and integrated into smart home systems to alert users when specific temperatures are reached.

item.title: OpenFlaps project provides open-source design for 3D-printed split flap displays
item.description:
Source: Hackaday Original headline: Another Split Flap Display You Can Print Yourself
Ivan has released OpenFlaps, an open-source design for a 3D-printed split flap display. The project uses a Raspberry Pi Pico W to manage time, coordinate flap movements, and provide a Wi-Fi web interface for remote control. Each individual flap assembly contains an ATtiny85 microcontroller and a 28BYJ-48 stepper motor that rotates a wheel containing 45 individually printed flaps. The hardware also includes provision for a BME280 sensor to monitor temperature, pressure, and humidity. The display is capable of showing text, time, and other data. Because the project is released under CC BY-SA 4.0 or MIT licenses, users can modify the design to suit specific needs. This project offers a way to build large-scale split flap displays, which were previously common in airport terminals and alarm clocks.

item.title: SIGMA Regen Superbike develops all-wheel-drive prototype for future Le Mans racing
item.description:
Source: New Atlas Original headline: 340-hp AWD Fireblade superbike targets Le Mans
French engineering project SIGMA Regen Superbike has unveiled the LMT02, an electric superbike prototype based on the Honda CBR1000RR-R Fireblade. The prototype features a proprietary Front Wheel Energy Recovery System (SRERA) that adds an electric drive and energy-recovery arrangement to the front wheel, creating an all-wheel-drive configuration. This system aims to harvest braking energy at the front tire, where weight shifts during deceleration, and could potentially recover up to 33% of the battery's energy. The project follows the LMT01 test bed and aims to challenge the electric motorcycle lap record at the Bugatti Circuit in Le Mans. Future development includes the LMR02, which targets a 250 kW (340 hp) output and an 800-volt electrical architecture, as part of an ambition to enter the 24 Hours of Le Mans in 2029. The team is also developing a quick-change battery arrangement and needs to raise an additional €190,000 (US$207,157) to fund upcoming development stages.

item.title: X adds native post scheduling or up to 18 months ahead to Android app
item.description:
Source: Digital Trends Original headline: X is finally letting Android users schedule posts up to 18 months ahead
X is adding native post scheduling to its Android app, allowing users to prepare posts up to 18 months in advance. While the website has supported scheduling since 2020 and the iPhone app received the feature earlier this year, Android users previously had to use the website or third-party services to schedule content. Engineer Evgenii Matsiuk announced Thursday that Android users can now attach photos or videos and select a future publication date or time. Scheduled posts will appear in the Drafts section, where users can edit content or change publication settings, or discard edits using a "Save changes" prompt. Once a post is scheduled, X handles the publication in the background and sends a notification to the user. This update follows a decision to rebuild the Android app from scratch in July, a process former X product head Nikita Bier said would allow the company to release new features faster.

item.title: WhatsApp to allow direct purchase and installation of travel data eSIMs
item.description:
Source: Digital Trends Original headline: WhatsApp’s new travel eSIM feature could save you a trip to the airport SIM counter
WhatsApp will soon allow users to purchase and install travel data eSIMs directly within the messaging app. This new feature aims to simplify international travel by removing the need to visit separate websites or download additional apps to secure a mobile data connection. WhatsApp is partnering with several telecom operators and eSIM providers, including Verizon, Jio, Smart Axiata, and Smart Communications, to offer this service. Once implemented, users can install an eSIM in a few taps and continue using the app with their existing phone number even while connected through a different SIM. While existing services like Airalo and Nomad already permit mobile eSIM purchases, WhatsApp's integration provides a more streamlined workflow. The company has not yet disclosed specific pricing, data allowances, or supported countries. A rollout is expected to begin in select markets soon, though users must ensure their hardware supports eSIM technology.

item.title: SALES: MIT Technology Review opens nominations for 2027 Innovators Under 35 competition
item.description:
Source: MIT Technology Review Original headline: Our 2027 Innovators Under 35 competition is now open
MIT Technology Review has opened nominations for its 2027 Innovators Under 35 competition. Each year, editors select 35 top young scientists, entrepreneurs, and inventors who are engineering solutions to global challenges such as climate change and human disease. Nominees must be able to demonstrate real-world impact through scientific discoveries, technological breakthroughs, or useful inventions. To qualify, a nominee must be under the age of 35 as of October 1, 2027, meaning they must have been born on or after October 2, 1992. Nominations must be submitted by 11:59 p.m. Eastern time on Tuesday, January 19. Following the deadline, editors will review nominees to select a group of semifinalists, who will then complete a formal application. A panel of expert judges will ultimately evaluate those applicants to select the final list. The publication has produced this annual list since 1999 to identify rising stars in various technical fields.

item.title: XPeng plans to sell IRON humanoid robot at price of an EV
item.description:
Source: Digital Trends Original headline: China’s Xpeng wants to put an eerily friendly humanoid robot in your home for the same price as an affordable EV
Chinese electric vehicle maker XPeng plans to release its IRON humanoid robot to the public in the second quarter of 2027. Vice Chairman Brian Gu told Bloomberg that the robot could be priced around the median selling price of an EV. Before the public launch, the robot is scheduled to begin training as a retail assistant at XPeng stores during the first quarter of 2027, with the company targeting sales of tens of thousands of units that year. The IRON robot features 76 degrees of freedom, 1,500 tactile sensing points, and three in-house Turing AI chips. It can navigate autonomously, accept voice or app-based tasks, recharge itself, and monitor its own health. XPeng intends to deploy the robot in commercial environments first, followed by industrial applications, before eventually moving into homes. Gu suggested household deployment could begin one to two years after successful commercial use, pending safety testing involving children, elderly people, and pets. The company also anticipates recurring revenue through software subscriptions, upgrades, and services.

item.title: X introduces parental safety controls for teen users aged 13 to 17
item.description:
Source: Digital Trends Original headline: X is finally getting robust parental controls to keep teens safe. It’s about time.
X, owned by Elon Musk, has announced new parental safety controls for users aged 13 to 17. These tools allow parents to monitor time spent on the platform, set daily limits, and require approval for new followers, which automatically makes the teen's account private. Parents can also limit the 'For You' feed to only show content from accounts a teen already follows, filter specific words, and disable sensitive media. While parents can see who a teen is messaging via the rebranded XChat, they cannot see the actual message content, searches, or viewing history. A parent can supervise up to five accounts, but supervision ends automatically when a teen turns 18. These updates follow criticism regarding content safety, including a report from the Center for Countering Digital Hate finding that sexually explicit content is easily accessible to 13-year-old accounts. Additionally, legal challenges from regulators like Ofcom and certain state attorneys general allege that the platform's Grok AI chatbot has helped proliferate non-consensual sexual images and child sexual abuse material.

item.title: Fraxinas builds automated terrarium that simulates New Caledonian weather conditions
item.description:
Source: Hackaday Original headline: Location-Accurate Weather For Your Gecko
Fraxinas has developed a specialized terrarium designed to simulate the specific weather conditions of New Caledonia. Controlled by an ESP32, the system manages lights, a heater, a misting pump, and fans to replicate real climate data from the island. Because the device is located in Germany, the system replicates conditions from six months prior to account for the seasonal offset between Germany and the South Pacific. While the original gecko for whom the device was built has passed away, the terrarium has since been repopulated with a new inhabitant. This transition included hardware upgrades, specifically improved lighting to support plant growth and safer materials to ensure a more secure environment for the gecko. This project represents a move beyond standard automated terrariums by attempting to follow a real-world habitat's climate patterns.

item.title: X mobile app adds new photo editing and typography tools
item.description:
Source: Digital Trends Original headline: X’s photo editor gains new tools, now at par with basic photo editors
X, formerly known as Twitter, has added a suite of photo editing tools to its mobile app, allowing users to refine images directly before posting. The update includes an Adjust panel with options for Lux, Brightness, Contrast, Saturation, Warmth, Color, Fade, and Highlights. Users can also apply preset filters or use an eyedropper tool to pull specific colors from an image. New typography features allow users to type captions directly over images using styles such as Basic, Strong, Typewriter, and Poster. To help hide or focus on specific details, the update provides tools to blur certain areas and a pinch-to-zoom function for precise subject selection. These updates aim to make X a central hub for content creation by reducing the need for third-party photo editing applications.

item.title: Kodak releases SlideTag photo display and location tracker keyring
item.description:
Source: New Atlas Original headline: Pocketable mini screen shows photos in E Ink & doubles as an AirTag
Kodak has released the SlideTag, a 1.54-inch E Ink keyring designed to display photos or other digital content. Modeled after 1935-era Kodachrome slide mounts, the device features a six-color 240x240 pixel screen. Users can upload photos or albums of up to 12 images via the Memory Link mobile app, which can also display to-do lists, contact information, dates, or QR codes. The SlideTag functions as a location tracker compatible with Apple's Find My and Google's Find Hub networks, and it can emit a 75 dB beep to assist in locating the device. It is water and dust resistant, uses Bluetooth 5.4, and runs on a replaceable CR2032 battery that may last up to a year. The product is sold in blind boxes featuring one of nine frame designs. Individual units retail for US$34.99, while an eight-piece box set is available for $279.92 via Amazon and Kodak's Reto site.

item.title: Amoeba Tech plans to release keyring-sized handset designed to reduce screen time
item.description:
Source: New Atlas Original headline: Is this keyring 'amoeba' the ultimate dumb phone?
Amoeba Tech, a company based in Troy, New York, is developing the Amoeba One, a keyring-sized handset designed to reduce screen time. The device features a stainless steel touchscreen housed in a colorful silicone exterior and a 360-degree rotating camera. It runs a custom Android-based OS with a curated app library for messaging, banking, maps, and audio streaming. Users can use the device as a primary phone via a physical SIM slot or as a companion device to a primary smartphone. Amoeba offers a service plan for $15 a month for unlimited 4G talk, text, and data, or a $1 trial month. The device includes a 1,000-mAh battery and supports Bluetooth connectivity. The product, which successfully met its crowdfunding goal in 30 minutes, is priced at $99, with special designs costing more. The company aims to begin shipping units next October.
